absent: Locking, concurrency and lifetime rules for management messages, telemetry buffers and virtualization state are not shown.
Error codes, timeout and retry behaviour for management commands are not shown.
Bootloader validation and population rules beyond layout, offsets and sentinel handling are not shown.
Debug trap delivery, privilege checks and register access sequences are not shown.
Firmware map construction, overlap handling and kernel reservation policy beyond type codes are not shown.
Virtualization ioctl numbers, call order and state transition rules for register and interrupt structures are not shown.
Units, scaling, sampling period and wrap behaviour for metric accumulators and bandwidth counters are not shown.
Selection effects and platform detection for hardware subarchitectures are not shown.

findings.text: Userspace reaches the management interface through two ioctl operations sharing one base number. The first exchanges a message descriptor in both directions on subcommand zero. The second supplies telemetry request parameters on subcommand one and depends on a companion request structure holding a buffer reference plus size and socket selector.
The common management ioctl base value is 248 decimal, 0xF8. Subcommand zero identifies the bidirectional message operation and subcommand one identifies the telemetry operation.

The metric snapshot is a fixed order record of 32 bit counters and 64 bit accumulators grouped by domain. It opens with a sample counter, then temperature maxima and their accumulators for socket and regulator and stacked memory, then socket power limit and ceiling and reading, then a timestamp with energy accumulators for socket and compute and graphics and interconnect and memory domains, then frequency limits and instantaneous clocks with small per-clock arrays of length four plus larger accumulator arrays of length eight for graphics and length ninety six for core clocks, then allowed frequency ranges with associated tables of length four and dynamic range bounds, then interconnect width and rate with per-link read and write bandwidth accumulators of length eight, then residency and utilization plus bandwidth accumulators and a peak memory bandwidth, then throttler residencies with a spare word, and finally an appended graphics frequency array of length eight that preserves compatibility by growing only at the end.

The telemetry request is a compact four field record. It carries a 64 bit buffer reference followed by a 32 bit length, then a 16 bit socket selector and a 16 bit reserved word that remains unused in this fragment.

Each tabulated management command is characterized by an input word count, an output word count and a direction class. The shown entries request either zero or one input word and return zero to three output words. Read style commands use a get class, the sideband write uses a set class, and floor limit and power and quality of service controls use a combined set-or-get class where one argument word encodes both the request and the reply.

Several combined commands multiplex suboperations inside one argument word. Floor control uses the top two bits to choose among per-core update, all-cores update, configured value query and effective value query, with processor identity in the middle bits and megahertz value in the low bits; frequency input is ignored on queries and the reply is only meaningful on queries. Sideband power limit uses the top bit to distinguish update from query with the remaining low bits holding the limit. Traffic priority and floating bandwidth commands similarly partition the word into operation and selector and parameter subfields, returning either capability discovery bits or current settings across one or two reply words.

The x86 auxiliary vector defines two tags. The system call entry address tag has value thirty two and the vector system call image header tag has value thirty three. The architecture vector extension size is three in one configuration and two in the alternate configuration.
The listed header guard symbols only prevent repeated inclusion. They carry no numeric ABI value, layout or behaviour in these fragments.
The bits-per-long width is sixty four in the 64 bit alternative and thirty two in the 32 bit alternative.
Three boot video selectors are defined. Normal text mode has value 0xFFFF, extended text mode has value 0xFFFE, and the interactive prompt selector has value 0xFFFD.

Ramdisk control packs a start mask of 0x07FF with a prompt flag bit 0x8000 and a load flag bit 0x4000. Loader capability bits include loaded-high at bit zero, address randomization at bit one, quiet at bit five, segment preservation at bit six and heap usability at bit seven. Extended loader flags cover 64 bit kernel, loading above four gigabytes, 32 and 64 bit firmware handover, firmware kexec, five level paging availability and enablement, and memory encryption at bits zero through seven respectively.

The setup header is a packed bootloader to kernel handshake with a fixed field order and no padding. It progresses from legacy sector and flag and size and console and device fields through signature and version and switch and segment descriptors, then loader type and flags and move size and protected mode entry, then ramdisk location and size and legacy kludge, then heap end and extended loader identity, then command line and address limits and alignment and relocatability, then command length and subarchitecture selectors and payload location and length, then setup chain reference and preferred address and initialization size and handover and info offsets. A companion descriptor table holds a sixteen bit length followed by fourteen raw bytes.

Two packed firmware records are defined. The laptop firmware header carries a magic value with version plus callback handle plus interrupt table reference. The firmware information record carries loader signature plus system table address split into low and high parts plus descriptor size and version plus memory map address split into low and high parts plus map size.

The zero page is a packed structure with architecturally fixed offsets. It starts with console info at zero and firmware power info nearby, then padded fields leading to measured launch address and processor inventory info and power management table address, then obsolete disk buffers and descriptor area and laptop header, then extended ramdisk and command line fields with a large pad, then a confidential blob address, then display and firmware records, then alternate memory size and scratch word, then single byte counts for memory map and disk parameter and signature entries plus keyboard and secure boot status, then a sentinel byte near 0x1EF and the setup header near 0x1F1 with padding to 0x290, then a signature buffer, then a 128 entry memory map at 0x2D0, then padding and disk parameter array and trailing pad to the end.

A nonzero sentinel value of 0xFF placed by early setup detects an overeager bootloader that copied beyond the setup header into a fresh zero page. When the sentinel is still set the kernel must treat portions of the page as invalid and clear the affected regions rather than trusting them.

The zero page memory map holds at most one hundred twenty eight entries. The jailhouse setup interface requires version one. The hardware subarchitecture enumeration assigns zero to generic PC, one to lguest, two to Xen, three to Intel mobile, four to CE4100, with the following value marking the count.

Debug address registers occupy indices zero through three, with status at index six and control at index seven. Status reserves mask 0xFFFF0FF0 and defines trap indicators for the four breakpoints at bits zero through three with their union, plus bus lock at bit eleven, single step at bit fourteen and task switch at bit fifteen.

Breakpoint control skips sixteen low bits and allocates four control bits per register. Access type encodings are zero for execution, one for write and three for read. Length encodings are zero for one byte, four for two bytes, twelve for four bytes and eight for eight bytes. Enablement uses two bits per register with local at shift zero and global at shift one, base values one and two, and aggregate masks 0x55 for all local enables and 0xAA for all global enables. Reserved control masks are 0xFC00 in the narrow alternative and 0xFFFFFFFF0000FC00 in the wide alternative. Pipeline slowdown uses 0x100 locally and 0x200 globally.

The firmware map is anchored at offset 0x2D0 with at most one hundred twenty eight entries and its count lives at offset 0x1E8. Type codes assign one to usable RAM, two to reserved, three to ACPI reclaimable, four to nonvolatile ACPI, five to unusable, seven to persistent memory, twelve to persistent RAM and one hundred twenty eight to kernel reserved. Legacy ranges place the option ROM hole from 0xA0000 to 0x100000 with BIOS aliases for the same span and the ROM image from 0xFFE00000 to 0xFFFFFFFF.
Each memory range descriptor is packed as a 64 bit base plus 64 bit length plus 32 bit type. The map wrapper holds a 32 bit entry count followed by an inline array sized by the architecture maximum.
An extended feature component is a packed four word descriptor carrying a type tag plus byte size plus byte offset plus flags, in that order.
Two second word hardware capability bits are shown. The user wait instruction bit is bit zero and the segment base instruction bit is bit one.
The speed step record holds four 32 bit words for signature plus command plus event plus performance level.

Virtualization shared pages use small page indices one for port input output, two for coalesced device writes and sixty four for dirty logging. The fragment also assigns conventional x86 trap numbers including zero for divide, one for debug, three for breakpoint, four for overflow, five for bound, six for invalid opcode, seven for device unavailable, eight for double fault, ten through fourteen for segment and protection faults, sixteen through twenty one for floating and alignment and machine and SIMD and virtualization exceptions, plus twenty eight through thirty for hypervisor and control and security exceptions.

Presence macros advertise which emulated facilities the x86 module implements, covering timer and input output interrupt controllers and interrupt lines and message interrupts and user nonmaskable interrupts and extended message interrupts and machine checks and extended timer state and Xen guest support and event injection and debug registers and extended state and control registers.

Fixed virtualization limits include two hundred fifty six interrupt vectors, a one kilobyte local APIC register image, twenty four input output APIC pins, three interrupt chips, sixteen filter ranges and a maximum filter bitmap of 0x600 bytes.

Programmable interrupt state is captured as edge detection and request and mask and service bytes plus priority and base and selection and poll and mode flags including special mask and init sequencing and auto end of interrupt and rotation and nesting and four byte init plus edge selection and its mask. The input output APIC state holds a base address plus selection and identifier plus pending bitmap with padding, then per-pin redirection entries that can be viewed as a raw 64 bit word or as decoded delivery and destination and status and polarity and trigger and mask fields with destination identity.

Interrupt chip selectors assign zero to master, one to slave and two to input output APIC. Execution run flags use bit zero for system management mode, bit one for bus lock trap and bit two for guest mode.
General register state transfers the sixteen 64 bit data and pointer registers together with instruction pointer and flags as one record used both when reading and when writing guest state.

Local APIC state is an opaque byte image sized by the register constant. A segment descriptor carries 64 bit base plus 32 bit limit plus 16 bit selector plus type and presence and privilege and mode flags plus an unusable marker. A system table descriptor carries 64 bit base plus 16 bit limit with padding.

System register state bundles six data segments plus task and local descriptors plus global and interrupt table pointers plus control registers zero two three four and eight plus extended feature register plus APIC base. The first variant appends an interrupt permission bitmap sized to cover all vectors. The second variant replaces that bitmap with a flags word plus four page directory pointer values whose validity is gated by a dedicated flag bit.

Floating state preserves eight 16 byte mantissa slots plus control and status words plus tag byte plus last opcode and instruction and data pointers plus sixteen 16 byte vector slots plus media control word with padding. A model specific register entry is a triple of 32 bit index plus reserved word plus 64 bit data.

Both model specific register containers are variable length records opened by a 32 bit count. The read-write form pads to alignment then appends that many register triples. The index-only form appends that many 32 bit identifiers without extra padding.

Filtering partitions the register space into up to sixteen ranges. Each range declares allowed directions with separate read and write bits, a base index, a length and a userspace bitmap where a set bit permits the declared directions and a clear bit denies them. The enclosing filter selects a global default of allow or deny and only the deny selection is valid in this fragment, with a mask defining the legal flag combinations.

Processor identification state uses counted flexible arrays. The legacy entry holds function plus four result words. The extended entry adds subleaf index and request flags with extra padding. The outer containers hold a count plus padding followed by the corresponding entries.
Extended identification flags use bit zero to mark a significant subleaf index, bit one to mark a stateful function and bit two to request the next stateful value.

Several structures embed untrusted sizes and addresses. The telemetry buffer reference plus length and socket index, the filter bitmap pointer plus range lengths, and the counted flexible arrays for registers and identifiers all require bounds and accessibility checks to avoid overread, overwrite or disclosure.

Packed boot layouts with explicit offsets and obsolete or reserved or spare fields must not be trusted blindly. Overlong bootloader copies signaled by the sentinel, stale disk and descriptor areas, and unchecked counts for memory map and disk parameters can corrupt early memory interpretation if used without sanitizing.
